**C.** Simultaneous hyperrotation and extension of the neck compromises the vertebral arteries, and the patient's confusion, nausea and vertigo point to vertebrobasilar insufficiency, so that technique error is what would make the physician liable. I don't accept the team note that cervical osteoarthritis is an absolute contraindication to neck treatment. It is a common finding at 78 and isn't an absolute contraindication, so option D doesn't establish liability. The other options describe acceptable technique.

CONFIDENCE: 88
